message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points are earned by winning rounds and are tallied from the cards left in opponents’ hands. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the Uno deck (108 cards).
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | | **Turn order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a reverse card is played). On your turn you may play one card that matches either the color or the symbol/number of the top discard. If you cannot play, you must draw one card. If that card can be played immediately, you may do so; otherwise the turn passes to the next player. | | **Special cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses direction of play.
• **Draw Two (+2)** – Next player draws two cards and misses a turn.
• **Wild** – You choose the new active color.
• **Wild Draw Four (+4)** – Same as Wild, but the next player also draws four cards. (Can only be played if you have no matching color; otherwise you risk being challenged.) | | **Winning a round** | When a player discards their last card they shout “Uno!” If they forget, the next player can call them out and force them to draw two cards. The round ends when a player has no cards left. | | **Scoring** | Add up the point values of all cards still held by the other players:
• Number cards = face value.
• Draw Two, Reverse, Skip = 20 points each.
• Wild, Wild Draw Four = 50 points each.
Points are added to the winner’s total. | | **Game end** | First player to reach the agreed‑upon score (e.g., 500) wins the game. | **Optional house rules** - *Stacking*: Some groups allow stacking +2/+4 cards (players can add to the penalty instead of drawing). - *No challenge*: Others ignore the “must have a matching color” rule for Wild Draw Four. - *Card‑draw penalties*: Some variations let you draw more than one card if you’re caught playing a Wild Draw Four illegally. Feel free to tweak or add house rules to suit your group!
